To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The agent can manage its risk by asking for bids in different settings of time constraints; (ii) The agent can maximize its expected profit by asking for bids that are “just right” in terms of the time constraints; (iii) The agent can use the model in a distributed setting, where it is the only agent that can evaluate bids and it is not aware of the bidding strategies adopted by the other agents.
(a) it is possible for an agent to manage its financial risk exposure by asking the right question, and (b) this requires the agent to know its risk posture and its utility function.

the risk of the agent can be modeled by Expected Utility Theory and that the model can be used by an agent to optimize its profits and manage its financial risk exposure when issuing a request for bids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How can an agent manage risk in the process of requesting bids for collections tasks?
the following question: how should a decision be made when it is not known how the decision will affect the decision maker's future?
the following questions: How should the request for bids be formulated?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a model that can be used by an agent to make decisions that are consistent with the preferences of its owner.
the model is useful for the problem it addresses.

the model is useful in situations where: the agent is interested in maximizing its profit; the agent is able to specify the probability of loss; the agent is not interested in maximizing its risk exposure; and the agent is able, in some way, to specify its risk tolerance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a framework that can be used by an agent to manage its risk exposure while requesting bids for complex collections of tasks.
the agent has to ask the right question, i.e., the one that maximizes the agent's profit while minimizing the risk of financial loss.
, in the context of multiagent contracting, the agent has to be able to ask the right question in order to get the right answer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the agent’s request for bids can be seen as the agent’s decision to commit resources in the future and that this decision is a risky decision.

, in order to be able to manage the risk of contracting with multiple agents, the contracting agent needs a model of the risk it faces, and a model that can be used in the context of multiagent contracting.
the risk posture of an agent is an important parameter in multiagent contracting, and should be taken into account when specifying a request for bids.
